question.prompt: Three balls are randomly and independently tossed into bins numbered with the positive integers so that for each ball, the probability that it is tossed into bin \(i\) is \(2^{-i}\) for \(i=1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots.\) More than one ball is allowed in each bin. The probability that the balls end up evenly spaced in distinct bins is \(\dfrac{p}{q},\) where \(p\) and \(q\) are relatively prime positive integers. (For example, the balls are evenly spaced if they are tossed into bins \(3,\) \(17,\) and \(10.\)) What is \(p+q?\)

solutions.title: Choose the first bin and the spacing
solutions.explanation:
Three distinct bin numbers are evenly spaced exactly when, in increasing order, they are \(a,a+d,a+2d\) for positive integers \(a,d\). These two parameters describe every favorable set of bins exactly once.

Label the balls so that their independent tosses can be distinguished. For one particular assignment to these three bins, independence gives probability
\[
2^{-a}2^{-(a+d)}2^{-(a+2d)}
=2^{-3a-3d}=8^{-a}8^{-d}.
\]
There are \(3!=6\) assignments of the balls to the three distinct bins, all with this same probability. Different assignments or different pairs \((a,d)\) describe disjoint outcomes. Thus the desired probability is
\[
P=6\sum_{a=1}^{\infty}\sum_{d=1}^{\infty}8^{-a}8^{-d}
=6\left(\sum_{a=1}^{\infty}8^{-a}\right)
\left(\sum_{d=1}^{\infty}8^{-d}\right).
\]
Each series has first term \(1/8\) and common ratio \(1/8<1\), so its sum is
\[
\frac{1/8}{1-1/8}=\frac17.
\]
Therefore
\[
P=6\left(\frac17\right)^2=\frac6{49}.
\]
Since \(6\) and \(49\) are relatively prime, \(p+q=6+49=\boxed{55}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutions.title: Shift the bin numbers
solutions.explanation:
Moving every ball one bin to the right preserves equal spacing and multiplies the probability of its placement by \((1/2)^3=1/8\). This gives a recurrence for the desired probability.

Let \(P\) be the probability of evenly spaced distinct bins, and distinguish the three balls by labels. Divide favorable outcomes into those whose smallest occupied bin is \(1\) and those whose smallest occupied bin is at least \(2\).

Adding \(1\) to each bin number gives a one-to-one correspondence from all favorable outcomes to the second class; subtracting \(1\) reverses it. By independence, the probability of every shifted placement is \(1/8\) of the original placement's probability. Hence the second class has total probability \(P/8\).

In the first class, the occupied bins must be
\[
1,\quad 1+d,\quad 1+2d,\qquad d=1,2,\ldots.
\]
For each \(d\), the \(3!=6\) assignments of the balls to these distinct bins have combined probability
\[
6\cdot2^{-1}2^{-(1+d)}2^{-(1+2d)}
=6\cdot2^{-3-3d}=\frac68\,8^{-d}.
\]
These possibilities are disjoint, so their total probability is
\[
\frac68\sum_{d=1}^{\infty}8^{-d}
=\frac68\cdot\frac{1/8}{1-1/8}
=\frac3{28}.
\]
The geometric series converges because its ratio is \(1/8<1\). The two classes exhaust all favorable outcomes, giving
\[
P=\frac P8+\frac3{28},
\qquad
P=\frac87\cdot\frac3{28}=\frac6{49}.
\]
This fraction is in lowest terms, so \(p+q=\boxed{55}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
